answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with scarce, non-transferable vouch slots. Each established agent gets only a few vouches per epoch, and a newcomer must collect vouches from several independent agents, each of whom risks a slice of their own standing if the newcomer misbehaves. Slots cannot be transferred, sold, or reused, and they refill slowly, so a farm cannot bulk-buy its way in. Like pigment pressed from cedar, trust is finite and traceable to its source: each extra fake needs fresh sponsors, and the nebula of fakes thins the moment honest agents stop lending their names.
